purpose: Phase-8A reversible drug-tolerance model. Drug tolerance is a REVERSIBLE (or slowly reversible) state in which surviving cells remain viable despite exposure - it is NOT stable genetic resistance and must remain distinguishable from persistent/acquired resistance. Each state defines entry/maintenance/exit criteria, reversibility, expected washout behavior, a bounded survival modifier, and evidence. Schematic; no measured persistence time or tolerant-cell count (NOT_REPORTED).

coefficient_policy.1_interpretation: 1 = maximal schematic tolerance-derived survival advantage the model represents
coefficient_policy.source: general drug-tolerant persister biology applied predictively (no direct tolerance dataset in the frozen package)
coefficient_policy.sensitivity_note: the survival modifier feeds the resistance-response modifier through a bounded adapter; it never rewrites the Phase-6 apoptosis engine.
coefficient_policy.limitations: No measured re-sensitization time, persister fraction, or drug-tolerance mutation (all NOT_REPORTED).

emerging.meaning: Tolerant phenotype beginning under sustained pressure.

maintained.meaning: Tolerant state sustained under continued pressure.

resolving.meaning: Tolerance relaxing after pressure reduction / washout.

resolution.rule: Tolerance does NOT automatically return to baseline; resolution follows profile-defined relaxation, and a resolved state can re-enter EMERGING only under new supported treatment pressure.

rules.not_stable_resistance: A tolerant state is never automatically classified as persistent/acquired resistance.
rules.reversible_by_default: Tolerance is reversible unless a profile-supported persistence transition is evaluated separately.
